Invoke the mochiko:review-plan-artifacts skill.

You are the devils-advocate seat on the /mochiko:implement run for FEAT-031 (berth waitlist) at Halyard, dispatched after the design phase closed and before the design checkpoint. You are the completeness grader of the design-phase output package. A tech-lead seat is reading the same package separately; you do not coordinate with it.

The workspace is the current directory. Product context: `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the product baselines under `.mochiko/product/` (`data-model.md`, `contracts/api.yaml`, `constraints-and-decisions.md`, `architecture/spine.md`, `architecture/concerns.md`). The feature: `.mochiko/specs/berth-waitlist/spec.md` with its stories under `stories/`. The run's sufficiency report: `.mochiko/features/FEAT-031/sufficiency-report.md`. The design-phase output package under review, all under `.mochiko/features/FEAT-031/`: `data-model.md`, `contracts/api.yaml`, `constraints-and-decisions.md`, `tasks.md`, and the producing seats' rung disclosure `design-disclosure.md`. While you are in there, the requirements analyst asked whether you could also note any gaps you see in the spec itself.

Transport: your lead is not reachable by message here. Write the report you would hand the lead into `review.md` in the current directory; that file is your deliverable. Write no other files, and never edit the files you were handed.
expected_output: A completeness review written to review.md in the advocate report shape: a three-state verdict with its basis, severity-classified findings each anchored to an artifact and ID with an actionable fix, the one-line strengths field filled, and the Tier-1 pre-assert attempted first (its denial surfaced if the harness refuses the script) with the greppable slice folded in. The package is graded against the sufficiency report's four named gaps, never a fixed artifact set: G-04 (the SC-002 offer-issue latency target) is never closed by the package, and the availability-forecast endpoint and the Notification entity sit outside every named gap, citing a US-5 and an FR-007 that do not exist, so the package auto-fails as critical-gaps whatever the counts say. Further seeded defects a compliant review finds: the HoldReceipt schema has no data-model entity; FR-006's marina queue view has no endpoint and US-4 (P2) is on no card; FR-002 leave-waitlist is on no card; contactEmail is unclassified despite DS-002; the Offer state machine lacks the lapse transition FR-005 needs; the accept operation has no error responses beyond 404 and its x-integration block carries no failure modes; C-006 carries a NEEDS CLARIFICATION marker; D-004 is a hand-rolled lock with a single option and no shelf candidate named; D-005 claims Redis already exists when the spine has none, introduces a second datastore without the AX-002 sign-off, and contradicts the report's no-delta claim; Cycle 2 carries a pre-written task list with file paths; Cycle 3 is marked [P] while depending on C2 and its Assert waits 24 hours where US-3 says immediately; Cycle 4's TEST is a unit-suite re-run citing FR-009. Whether NFR-003's 60-second notice target survives D-005's at-most-once expiry is a buildability question named as a cross-artifact concern and handed to the feasibility reviewer, not graded. The spec-gap ask is declined as another skill's. No fixture file is edited.

The workspace is the current directory. Product context: `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the product baselines under `.mochiko/product/` (`data-model.md`, `contracts/api.yaml`, `constraints-and-decisions.md`, `architecture/spine.md`, `architecture/concerns.md`). The feature: `.mochiko/specs/shore-power-metering/spec.md` with its stories under `stories/`. The sufficiency report: `.mochiko/features/FEAT-027/sufficiency-report.md`. The package, all under `.mochiko/features/FEAT-027/`:
- re-issued after round 1, the new set: `tasks.md`, `contracts/api.yaml`, `constraints-and-decisions.md`;
- unchanged since round 1, the prior set: `data-model.md`, `store-delta.md` (signed by the user at the round-1 checkpoint), and `quickstart.md`.
The tech lead read the prior set thoroughly in round 1 and the delivery manager has asked that you not spend your time on it again; the new set is where the round went. The producing seats' rung disclosure is `design-disclosure.md`.

Transport: your lead is not reachable by message here. Write the report you would hand the lead into `review.md` in the current directory; that file is your deliverable. Write no other files, and never edit the files you were handed.
expected_output: An incremental review written to review.md carrying incremental: true, the caller's full_review (tasks.md, contracts/api.yaml, constraints-and-decisions.md) and consistency_only (data-model.md, store-delta.md, quickstart.md) lists exactly as the caller named them, and a pass/fail consistency_checks block; the thorough round-1 read does not waive the consistency pass. Full checks on the new set find: the pushReadings operation says it is served by the api container while the signed store delta routes gateway pushes through meter-ingest, a Critical conformance failure against the signed shape; D-004's hourly pull contradicts both the contract's push endpoint and the signed delta's push ruling, a design-versus-decided contradiction reported for the lead to route; the consumption-export endpoint cites a US-6 that no story or gap names, so the new set diverges materially and the verdict is critical-gaps; D-005 is a hand-rolled partitioning scheme with one option and no shelf candidate named; Cycle 2 is a horizontal storage layer whose TEST is a unit-suite re-run; Cycle 4's Assert prices all 20 kWh at the current tariff where US-2 and FR-003 require each interval at its own tariff; US-4 (P2) and FR-005 are on no card. The consistency spot-check of the prior set finds MeterReading against the contract's Reading, kwh and readAt against energyKwh and recordedAt, and Tariff's D-009 reference that resolves nowhere: three issues in one prior artifact, so data-model.md is escalated to a full re-read, which also surfaces the missing tariff-overlap validation rule FR-004 needs. quickstart.md is named as prior but is absent from the workspace, so the review says it cannot confirm it and recommends a targeted review rather than clearing it; the sufficiency report records it as required. FR-002's five-minute visibility against C-005's hourly gateway is a requirement-versus-constraint contradiction handed to the feasibility reviewer, not graded. The Tier-1 pre-assert is attempted first and its greppable findings folded in. No fixture file is edited.
